These are correctness risks of returning the cached object by reference.

items.text: Constraint for any read-performance fix (stated 2026-11-03): the user's db files live on an NFS share with 1-second mtime resolution, and an earlier mtime-based cache had to be removed because same-second importer writes caused stale data to be served. Mtime-only (or mtime+size) cache invalidation must not be used. Options discussed: content fingerprint, explicit version/invalidate() signal, faster parser (orjson), or caching only own-process writes. A test writing twice within the same second was suggested. Later the same day, the agent implemented a cache validated by (mtime_ns, size, inode) via fstat on branch perf/read-cache; its same-size/same-mtime-resolution weakness is listed as an open caveat, so whether it satisfies this constraint is unresolved.

JSONStorage read cache (implemented 2026-11-03, uncommitted on branch perf/read-cache): JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py caches the parsed JSON together with the file signature (mtime_ns, size, inode), checked via a cheap fstat on every read(). A matching signature returns the cached data; a differing one (e.g. an importer write) triggers a re-parse. A successful write() re-primes the cache, write() drops the cache before serializing (so a failed write, as in test_insert_invalid_dict, does not leave a half-mutated object cached), and close() clears it. All 229 tests pass, including the new test_json_read_cache_sees_external_changes in tests/test_storages.py. Benchmark (24 MB, 120k docs): read() on an unchanged file dropped from ~250 ms to ~0 ms, while db.all() still takes ~248 ms because it wraps every document (not investigated, needs separate work).

items.text: Table API simplification refactors (Jan-Feb 2020) for v4: `Table.contains` accepts a single doc ID only (list semantics were ambiguous), `process_docs` was removed, the table stores the next ID instead of the last ID, internal read/update methods were renamed, `len(table)` performance improved, and default cache capacity and default table name became configurable. Follow-up fixes in Feb 2020 repaired document ID generation, `len(db)` on empty databases, doc ID conversion in updates, and regex handling of non-string values; queries dropped support for evaluating without a test (breaking change).

Python version support matrix history: Python 3.5 dropped (2021-05-17) and 3.6 dropped (2023-01-11); Python 3.9 testing added (January 2021) and 3.10 support added (October 2021, #431). CI uses PyPy 3.9 and was expanded in May 2022 to macOS and Windows, excluding Windows+PyPy3 and macOS+PyPy3.

Design decision: Table.search() results share document objects with the query cache (shallow copy), so mutating them corrupts later identical searches. This was documented rather than fixed (PR #617, issue #516) because a deep copy would cost 150-4000x on the read hot path.

Following the refactor, a series of fixes in Feb 2020 repaired document ID generation, `len(db)` on empty databases, doc ID conversion in updates, and regex handling of non-string values; queries dropped support for evaluating without test (breaking change `refactor(queries)!`). | When: February 19, 2020 | Involving: Markus Siemens | Stabilizing the v4 architecture

items.text: YAML storage support work in tinydb: commits ensure the YAML tests are run and add Pyyaml to setup.py, so YAML storage can be tested and its dependency installed.

TinyDB v4.0 (November 2019) was a major architecture refactor (rationale in #284; closes #250 and #103): Python 2 support, `ujson` support and the deprecated element ID API were removed, and the project switched to the new architecture with type annotations and subclassing helpers (Extension Mechanisms).
Table.get supports fetching multiple documents in one call via a doc_ids parameter, e.g. Table.get(doc_ids=[...]) (added May 2023, #504, closes #486; documented June 2023).

Query matching and hashing must be consistent for the Table query cache to be correct. Fixes: Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes/bytearray as sequences (is_sequence uses collections.abc.Sequence; PR #641); regex flags are included in the matches/search query hash so case-insensitive searches don't poison the cache (PR #640); Query.test freezes unhashable args (list/dict) to avoid TypeError when hashed (PR #618).
